title: Onco Owl – Pediatric Oncology: Optimizing Clinical Workflows and Lived Care
summary:
Background
Every year, around 2,250 children and adolescents in Germany are diagnosed with cancer. The disease and the often lengthy treatment place a heavy burden on the children, adolescents, and their families. In addition to physical complaints, emotional problems, worries, difficulties at school, and social isolation can also arise. Frequent hospital stays and prolonged absences from school cause many children to lose contact with friends and teachers. Parents and siblings are also under considerable strain and often find the situation emotionally and financially stressful. Previous studies have mainly focused on the period after treatment has been completed. Less is known about how children, adolescents, and their parents experience the support they receive at the beginning of treatment. This early phase is particularly challenging and can be decisive in determining how well families are able to cope with the disease.

Research question
The study examines how children and adolescents with cancer and their parents perceive the care they receive during the first phase of treatment. Four different areas are examined:

1. Hospital
2. Family
3. School
4. Additional support

The aim is to identify strengths and possible gaps in care at an early stage. On this basis, ways of improving care for affected families will be developed.

Method
The study is being conducted at several university hospitals in Germany. Parents of children and adolescents with cancer, as well as affected children and adolescents aged 10 to 21 who were diagnosed no more than two years ago and are still undergoing intensive treatment, are eligible to participate. The survey is conducted online, with both children and adolescents and their parents completing separate questionnaires.
conditions: Care for children and adolescents with cancer and their families during the acute phase of treatment

interventions.name: Parents of children and adolescents with cancer

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children and adolescents
•Children and adolescents (aged 10–21) with cancer (not further defined)
•Initial diagnosis no more than two years ago
•Therapy: acute phase
•Sufficient language skills to answer the questionnaire
•Language: native-level German
•Stable internet access

Parents
•Parents or legal guardians of a child (0–21 years) with cancer (not further defined)
•Initial diagnosis no more than 2 years ago
•Therapy: acute phase
•Sufficient language skills to answer the questionnaire
•Stable internet access
Exclusion criteria:
Children and adolescents
•Excessive physical or psychological stress

Parents
•Excessive physical or psychological stress
